hero.title: A Fairer Catch.
hero.label: A Stronger Coast.
hero.text: Enhancing livelihoods through locally developed approaches to reduce illegal fishing practices. Across five Beach Management Units in the KAMAMKUKI Joint Co-Management Area, communities are shaping solutions that protect the sea and create more inclusive ways to earn a living.

impactBand.text4: When communities thrive, the ocean has room to recover.

theChallenge.heading: Healthy Waters. Secure Livelihoods.
theChallenge.text: Illegal fishing is putting pressure on fish stocks, marine habitats, and the families who depend on the sea. Gear exchange efforts can fall short when communities do not shape and own the solutions. In KAMAMKUKI, five fishing communities are working together to co-manage 25 km² of nearshore habitat, where dragnetting remains a challenge.
theChallenge.text2: This project puts local leadership at the centre: reducing harmful gear and practices while building skills and opening up diversified income opportunities for fishers, women, youth, and people with disabilities.
theChallenge.imageAlt: A fisher on the Kenyan coast carrying his nets

designedToInclude.heading: Opportunity Should Reach Everyone
designedToInclude.imageAlt: Community members at a training session
designedToInclude.text: Half of the 200 community members to be trained are women. The project's 695 direct IPLC beneficiaries and their households, an estimated 4,164 people, are projected to benefit from healthier ecosystems and stronger fisheries.

theBiggerPicture.heading: A Better Future for People and the Sea
theBiggerPicture.text: By supporting community-owned solutions, the initiative aims to restore habitats, improve fish stocks, strengthen incomes, and inspire approaches that can travel beyond the coast.

callToAction.heading: Support Community-Led Change
callToAction.text: Your support helps fishing communities replace harmful practices with livelihoods that last.
